svg.title: Internet's protocols — study visual
svg.desc: Study guide on TCP/IP, packet switching, and IPv4 vs IPv6
svg.text: Unit 10 · Text 4 — TCP/IP, packet switching, IPv4 vs IPv6

g.text: Data is broken into small packets. Each packet sent individually across the Net by routers.
Puts each packet in an envelope
Tells the Internet where to send data

svg.text: How TCP works — step by step

g.text: 1. Data broken into packets of fewer than 1,500 characters each
2. Header added to each packet + checksum calculated (detects errors introduced during transmission)
3. Each packet put in IP envelope with addressing info → routers examine and determine most efficient path
4. Packets travel through series of routers — may arrive OUT OF ORDER (traffic load changes constantly)
5. On arrival: TCP calculates checksum. If checksums don't match → packet corrupted → retransmit
6. Non-corrupt packets reassembled into original, unified form
IPv4's ~4.3 billion addresses were nearly exhausted. IPv6 provides vastly more to support growth of the Internet.
Small chunk of data sent individually
